effect.note: Clause uses 'may' and says the customer is entitled to return only within 90 days with proof of purchase; the merchant discretion beyond these conditions is not encoded. Refund form assumed as the return remedy; amount not stated.

rules.description: Return within 90 days of purchase with valid proof of purchase is permitted (entitlement, discretionary wording noted).

effect.note: Clause says 'exclusions apply' without specifying them; amount limited to merchandise (subtotal) excluding shipping and tax. Refund method is original payment. Exclusions are unspecified so rule may need human review.

rules.description: Merchandise returned with valid proof of purchase receives a refund to the original form of payment, for merchandise only (exclusions not specified in clause).

effect.note: Clause states returns are not accepted without valid proof of purchase. Applied to return-type claim reasons; the clause does not name a specific reason list, so the list reflects return-type claims.

rules.description: Deny return/refund claims when the customer lacks proof of purchase

effect.note: Clause is discretionary ('in Rockler's discretion'); refund reduced by Rewards Card amount redeemed. Gift Cards excluded per clause but gift_card is a distinct payment_method value. Void-if-unused alternative not encodable without usage fact.

rules.description: Return of order paid partly with promotional Rewards Card: at Rockler's discretion, refund reduced by the Rewards Card amount redeemed (requires human discretion).

effect.note: Clause states a condition for full refund (all components included) but does not state the outcome when components are missing or whether component completeness is an ontology fact. No ontology field captures component completeness, so the rule cannot be decided from facts; escalate for human judgme

rules.description: Full refund on returned merchandise requires all components included; this is a condition on full refund only, so a partial-refund reduction applies when components are missing.

effect.note: Clause allocates shipping charges only; no refund or remedy amount is stated. Encoded as customer-paid return shipping for non-damaged, non-defective items. The remedy is none because the clause sets no amount.

rules.description: Customer pays return shipping charges unless the item is damaged or defective (customer-responsibility default)

effect.note: Clause lists clearance items as non-returnable; mapped to is_final_sale. Software and downloadable plans are not separately captured as a fact in the ontology except via category 'plan' and 'clearance', so those are covered in a companion rule.

rules.description: Software, downloadable plans and clearance items are non-returnable: deny returns when the item is final sale.

effect.note: Downloadable plans are non-returnable per clause; category 'plan' used as proxy.

rules.description: Downloadable plans (item category 'plan') are non-returnable.

effect.note: Clearance items are non-returnable per clause; category 'clearance' used as proxy.

rules.description: Clearance items (item category 'clearance') are non-returnable.

effect.note: Clause says promotional gift card is voided if unused. Modeled as partial with no monetary remedy; the void is a deduction-type outcome not in the remedy enum. Condition 'new_unopened' used as proxy for unused; ontology has no explicit unused flag for gift cards.

rules.description: Promotional gift card (gift card with purchase) unused: void the gift card on refund

effect.note: Clause sets an authorization requirement only; no remedy or amount stated. Direct ship items are not covered by an ontology fact and are not encoded.

rules.description: Power tools require authorization on all returns; the clause does not state an outcome, so a human must authorize.

effect.note: Clause says non-warranty returns must be unused and in original packaging. Applied to change_of_mind claims only; warranty/defect claims are outside this clause. Denial reason inferred from the requirement's negation.

rules.description: Non-warranty returns must be unused and in original packaging; returns that are not unused/original packaging are denied.

effect.note: Exclusion: non-returnable brand and class. Clause says Sawstop; matched as SawStop brand.

rules.description: Laguna and SawStop power tools are non-returnable

effect.note: Clause says 'fails to perform for any reason'; no proof of purchase required, so receipt is not a requirement. Brand and condition not conditioned by clause.

rules.description: Router bit that fails to perform is replaced; no proof of purchase required

effect.note: Clause covers Rockler TopSlide/Centerline Lifetime drawer slides that fail to perform for any reason; replacement issued without proof of purchase. Eligibility keyed to lifetime guarantee flag and drawer_slide category.

rules.description: Drawer slide lifetime guarantee: failed Rockler drawer slide replaced with no proof of purchase required

effect.note: Clause RK-RET-14: clearance items sold as final sale are not eligible for return. Applied as an exclusion; claim_reasons left open since clause does not restrict by claim reason.

rules.description: Clearance/final-sale items are not eligible for return (exclusion).

effect.note: Clause specifies refund method (original payment) for store returns; the store-location channel itself is not an ontology fact, so the rule applies on the refund method only.

rules.description: Merchandise returned to a Rockler store location is refunded to the original payment method.

effect.note: Clause excludes original shipping charges from refund; amount is order total less shipping paid, assuming the remaining refund base is the merchandise and tax. Tax treatment is not stated, so confidence is moderate.

rules.description: Original shipping charges are not refunded on returns.

effect.note: Clause says stores can only issue a Rockler gift card for these tenders. Mapped to store_credit as the closest remedy in the enum. Apple Pay has no distinct payment_method enum value in the ontology, so it is not encoded. Clause does not state a refund amount.

rules.description: Refunds for purchases made with Apple Pay or PayPal are issued as a Rockler gift card; the clause describes a payment processing constraint, which is a refund-form statement tied to tender type.

effect.note: Clause says cancellation allowed any time before pickup. Mapped pickup to has_shipped as closest ontology fact; pickup is not a defined field, so confidence reduced.

rules.description: Customer may cancel order before it has been picked up (not yet shipped).

effect.note: Clause refers to pickup, which is not an ontology fact; condition approximated using order status and days since order. Refund follows cancellation; amount not specified so left null.

rules.description: Order not picked up after 5 days is automatically cancelled and refunded

effect.note: Refund equals merchandise amount in original payment form; shipping (order.shipping_total) excluded. Store-return channel is assumed by the clause only as a return to a store location; no store-location fact exists in the ontology, so the condition is tested on payment method presence.

rules.description: Store return of merchandise receives refund in original form of payment; original shipping charges are not refunded.
